subject: Geography
title: Social and Economic Development
learningOutcomes: Define development as social and economic welfare, and distinguish Economic Development Indicators (EDI) from Human Development Indicators (HDI).
Investigate key economic indicators — GDP, PPP, economic condition, education, health, trade, industrialisation, political stability and wildlife.
Describe the Human Development Index: its three dimensions and four indicators, and evaluate Pakistan’s position.
Explain how inflation and unemployment affect the development of a country.
Evaluate the impact of technology and the Industrial Revolution, and the role of the OECD.

sections.heading: What is Development?
sections.body: Development is the improvement in people’s freedom to choose and the expansion of their capabilities, so that people can meet their basic needs and live a comfortable, satisfying life. When people are economically sound, the result is social welfare. Development refers to the aggregate of the satisfaction of all the individuals of a society and includes both social and economic welfare. It is measured through Economic Development Indicators (EDI) and Human Development Indicators (HDI); inflation and unemployment are the two factors that affect it.

sections.heading: Economic Development Indicators – GDP & PPP
sections.body: GDP (Gross Domestic Product) is the total monetary or market value of all finished goods and services produced in a country during a specific time — the nation’s total economic output. GDP per capita is GDP and total product taxes divided by mid-year population. An increase in real GDP shows the economy is performing well. GDP at PPP (Purchasing Power Parity) is an exchange rate that removes the price-level difference between countries. By 2022 IMF estimates, the largest economies by PPP GDP were China, the US and India.

sections.heading: EDI – Economy, Education & Health
sections.body: A poor economic condition is shown by the percentage of population with income below basic needs, malnourishment, lack of safe drinking water and poor sanitation. A developed nation provides food, shelter, clean water and sanitation. Education is measured by literacy rate and mean years of schooling — an educated, skilled population develops faster. Health is measured by doctors per 1,000 people and life expectancy. The WHO recommends at least 2.5 medical staff per 1,000 people; Pakistan had 1.12 per 1,000 in the 2019 report.

sections.heading: EDI – Trade, Industry, Stability & Wildlife
sections.body: Quality infrastructure (roads, railways, airports) and open trade policies help nations flourish. Industrialisation matters: an economy that depends totally on agriculture is not well developed, while more manufacturing and less agriculture signals development. Political stability and security provide a conducive environment. Wildlife diversity brings pollinators, pest control, food supply, medicines and genetic resources, but is threatened by habitat loss and illegal trade.

sections.heading: Human Development Indicators (HDI)
sections.body: The HDI, designed by the UNDP, measures development using income, health and education and ranks countries by their level of development. Its three dimensions are Health, Education and Living standards. The four indicators are life expectancy at birth (Health), expected years of schooling and mean years of schooling (Education), and gross national income (GNI) per capita (Living standards).

sections.heading: Pakistan, Inflation, Unemployment, Technology & OECD
sections.body: Pakistan fell seven places to rank 161 of 192 on the HDI (2021-22); recent life expectancy is 66.1 years, expected schooling about eight years and GNI per capita $1,505, the drop caused by climate shocks like floods. Inflation is a rise in prices that reduces purchasing power (demand-pull and cost-push are its two causes). Unemployment causes health, economic and social harm and lowers GDP. Efficient technology raises productivity and GDP (Industry 1.0 steam/water → 4.0 Smart Factory). The OECD, founded in 1961 with 38 members, supports the economic and social welfare of people worldwide.

definitions.definition: Improvement in people’s freedom to choose and expansion of their capabilities to meet basic needs and live comfortably.
Gross Domestic Product — the total value of all finished goods and services produced in a country in a given time.
Purchasing Power Parity — an exchange rate that removes the price-level difference between countries.
Human Development Index — a UNDP tool measuring development through income, health and education.
Gross National Income per person — the Living standards indicator of the HDI.
A rise in the prices of goods and services that reduces the purchasing power of consumers and businesses.
Inflation caused when demand for goods is greater than the ability to produce them.
Inflation caused when the cost of raw material rises, raising the prices of final products.
People who do not have a source of income.
Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development — founded 1961, 38 members; supports economic and social welfare.

examTips: Learn the exact figures: WHO 2.5 medical staff per 1,000; Pakistan 1.12 (2019); HDI rank 161 of 192; OECD founded 1961 with 38 members.
Don’t mix up the two inflation types: demand-pull = demand exceeds production; cost-push = raw-material cost rises.
HDI = three dimensions (Health, Education, Living standards) and four indicators (life expectancy; expected + mean years of schooling; GNI per capita).
